title: The Preservation of the Scriptures
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Self-Authenticating Nature of Scripture
subpoints: The Bible is the ultimate authority and does not require external proof.
Evidences confirm, rather than prove, the claims the Bible makes about itself.
The focus shifts from apologetics to the internal witness of the text.

outline.title: Biblical Promises of Eternal Preservation
subpoints: Psalm 119:89 declares God's word is settled in heaven forever.
Isaiah 40:8 contrasts the fleeting nature of human glory with the permanence of God's word.
Matthew 24:35 affirms that Jesus's words (the entire Bible) will not pass away.
1 Peter 1:23-25 cites Isaiah to confirm the abiding nature of the gospel message.

outline.title: Confessional Affirmation of Purity
subpoints: The Westminster Confession affirms the Bible was kept pure by God's providence.
Original languages (Hebrew, Greek, Aramaic) are the standard for resolving controversies.
Translations are necessary for worship and understanding in every nation.

outline.title: Refuting the 'Game of Telephone' Analogy
subpoints: Manuscript transmission is written, not oral, allowing for verification.
Transmission occurs in multiple parallel lines, not a single chain.
Early copies can be compared directly to later ones to identify errors.

outline.title: The Masoretes and Textual Care
subpoints: Masoretes added vowel points to preserve pronunciation of Hebrew.
Scribes counted letters and words to ensure exact copying.
The Aleppo and Leningrad Codices represent the oldest complete Hebrew Bibles.

outline.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls as Confirmation
subpoints: Discovery of the Dead Sea Scrolls bridges the gap between the oldest codices and the original writing.
The scrolls confirm the high fidelity of the Masoretic text.
God's providence is evident in the preservation of these ancient documents.

summary:
This sermon continues the series on the reliability of the Bible, focusing specifically on the preservation of the Scriptures. The teaching begins by establishing that the Bible is self-authenticating; therefore, external evidences serve to confirm what the text already claims about itself rather than proving its authority. The pastor highlights several key passages, including Psalm 119:89, Isaiah 40:8, and Matthew 24:35, which collectively affirm that God's word is eternal, settled in heaven, and will not pass away. These biblical promises are reinforced by the Westminster Confession of Faith, which asserts that God's providence has kept the original texts pure in all ages.

The sermon addresses the common skepticism that centuries of hand-copying would have corrupted the text, comparing it to the game of telephone. This analogy is refuted by noting that manuscript transmission is written (allowing for checking), multi-linear (allowing for comparison across different copies), and verifiable against earlier links. A simplified example of a family recipe illustrates how multiple copies can be used to reconstruct the original with certainty, even if the original is lost.

Finally, the sermon examines the historical evidence for this preservation, particularly the work of the Masoretes who meticulously copied the Hebrew Old Testament, counting letters and words to ensure accuracy. While the oldest complete Hebrew codices date to the 10th century, the discovery of the Dead Sea Scrolls provides crucial evidence that the text remained stable for over a thousand years, confirming the biblical promise that God has faithfully preserved His word for the church today.
